function: GNN outputs BS beamforming (common and private), phase shifts of two RISs and common-rate allocation to maximize the sum-rate of an RSMA MISO system (p. 3-4).
system: RSMA downlink MISO: BS with M=2 antennas, K=4 single-antenna users, two passive reflecting RISs (L=10-50 elements, 4-bit phases); frequency band not stated (p. 2, 4).
method: GNN with initial, update and readout layers, unsupervised training with loss of negative sum-rate plus minimum-rate penalty, Adam optimizer, batch of 32 (p. 3-4).
data_channel: Simulated Rician BS-RIS and RIS-user links (mu=10), Rayleigh BS-user links, path-loss exponents in [2, 3.5]; random user positions generate CSI samples (p. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Random user positions; imperfect CSI, sigma^2 0.001 and 0.01; trained with K in {2,4,6,8,10} users and tested on each K (Table IV) (p. 4-5).
baselines: Learned: DL-based RSMA [10], GNN-based NOMA [9], original GNN model [9]; non-learned: SCA-based RSMA [11] (p. 4).
metrics: Sum-rate (bps/Hz) versus RIS elements and CSI error, running time in seconds, training convergence, sum-rate across train/test user counts (p. 4-5).
complexity: Measured running time (Table III): GNN-RSMA 0.008 to 0.045 s for L=10 to 50, SCA-RSMA 5.46 to 6.59 s; no operation or parameter count (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 2: "The BS-to-user channels are modeled as Rayleigh"; the BS-RIS and RIS-user links are Rician with path-loss exponents (Eqs. 1-3, Table I on p. 4), a custom simulator with no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 5: "Table IV presents the generalization ability of the solution method based on GNN model under different numbers of testing and training users"; p. 5: "The GNN model maintains good performance for user sets of varying sizes".
q3_support: p. 4: "(iii) deep learning (DL) [10] based RSMA. (iiii) successive convex approximation (SCA) [11] based RSMA."; p. 4: "For perfect CSI, the GNN based RSMA outperforms the DL based one"; Fig. 3 plots the sum-rate of all schemes.
q4_support: p. 5: "Table III presents the running times of different schemes."; Table III lists measured seconds, 0.008 to 0.045 for GNN-RSMA against 5.461 to 6.592 for SCA-RSMA.
q5_support: p. 4: "The positions of users are randomly generated within the specified range"; the CSI samples come from the authors' own simulation, with no link, DOI, public dataset or measured data.
notes: Included: an unsupervised GNN jointly designs BS beamforming, RIS phase shifts and the RSMA common-rate allocation (area 3). q2 is met by Table IV, where models trained with one number of users are tested with other numbers of users; the imperfect-CSI sweep alone would not count. Fig. 3 compares SCA (non-learned), DL [10] and GNN-NOMA [9] on sum-rate; Table II compares with the original GNN [9] on sum-rate and running time. Title and DOI 10.1109/LCOMM.2025.3620747 are on p. 1.
